Brand &
typography.

An original identity built around the Phase 2 logo: confident blue, warm orange, and clear architectural lettering.

Precise. Capable. Approachable.

The core palette

Pale Blue #E6F0F7

Selection fill on light surfaces.

Sky #8BC4E8

Links and focus accents on dark surfaces.

70% neutrals and dark structure · 20% blue · 10% orange or clay. A starting balance for brand compositions, excluding photography. Working screens use less decorative color.

Blue leads

Keep actions, navigation, and selections consistently blue. Use Sky where light text is needed on dark navy.

Orange adds warmth

Choose one main warm detail per composition. Pair orange with white text; pair Clay and Sand with dark text.

Color has a purpose

Use labeled green, amber, and red states for success, attention, and errors. Keep decorative accents separate.

The blue is sampled from the existing logo. Supporting colors, typography, and usage rules are a proposed identity. Hex values describe digital sRGB colors; print work needs a proof.

Preserve the mark.

04 / Imagery, layout & voice

Give the identity room.

Use photography and a few deliberate brand details to give company materials character. Keep working screens calm and practical.

Both images are generated concepts. The photograph is not a company project; the blueprint illustration is decorative.

Architectural artwork, used with restraint.

Use fine matte-metal grain in the navy sidebar and finer grain in the slate top bar. Use the Jobs blueprint treatment across main page headers. Keep the texture subtle and uniform so navigation stays clear. Typography and warm selection accents carry the identity. Timecard navigation follows this identity; the green workspace retains its established appearance.

Consistent spacing

Build from 4px steps: 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, and 48px. Use larger gaps between sections than between related controls.

Appropriate emphasis

Company pages can use large imagery and headings. Carry the identity into the app with smaller, purposeful details.

Readable color

Use dark body text on Sand and Clay. Keep orange body text on white. Check text against each image crop.

Plain. Direct. Helpful.

“All changes saved.”   “Couldn’t save. Try again.”

Use familiar field names and a clear next step. Preserve the workflows people already know.

9.96 : 1White on Phase 2 Blue
4.94 : 1White on Burnt Orange
7.27 : 1Deep Ink on Soft Clay

Measured solid-color pairs. Target 4.5:1 for ordinary text and 3:1 for essential control boundaries. Validate actual screens and interaction states during implementation.

The visible guide records the current visual direction. Saira Semi Condensed headings and Source Sans 3 body text now appear in the core workspace. Blueprint artwork appears at sign-in and in the main page headers, using a shared right-aligned crop, subtle opacity, navy background, and short orange accent. The sidebar uses a subtle navy matte-metal texture, paired with a finer slate-metal top bar. The workspace canvas remains plain. Their green workspaces retain the established styles.

Condensed implementation reference

Consolidated September 9, 2026 from the former planning documents. This retains product constraints, architectural boundaries, and unresolved decisions. Detailed completed-refactor logs are historical evidence, not a new work queue. The current code, tests, and latest user instructions take precedence over older planning assumptions.

Current scope and order

  • Keep the application simple and preserve familiar labels, field order, navigation, and autosave behavior. Current work establishes an original Phase 2 identity around the logo; example websites inform taste, not a copied style.
  • Saira Semi Condensed with Source Sans 3 is now applied to the core workspace. The navy blueprint login background replaced the smoky artwork. The initial repeated blueprint treatment was simplified: architectural artwork is reserved for main page headers within the workspace, standardized from the approved Jobs header. Section headings and editor panes remain plain. Fine matte-metal grain defines the navigation: deep navy on the sidebar and finer slate grain on the top bar. Work surfaces remain plain. Shared workspace tokens standardize surfaces, controls, status colors, and selection accents. Continue future refinements within this boundary.
  • Style the navigation, outer background, dialogs, and notifications on timecard and export pages consistently with the app. Preserve the green workspaces: fonts, shared-style inheritance, controls, worksheet geometry, keyboard behavior, formulas, email/PDF rendering, CSV output, and two-cards-per-page print layout.
  • Keep the established UI flat and readable. Do not introduce extra settings, workflow modes, or features as part of styling. The guide's Save buttons illustrate appearance; existing autosave workflows keep their behavior.

Product and workflow rules

  • The app serves Jobs, Users, Employees, Timecards, Daily Logs, Shop Orders, Shop Catalog, and reference lists through role dashboards and shared job workspaces. Administrative setup uses the existing edit mode where appropriate.
  • Browsing dates, weeks, history, catalogs, or records must not create data. Creation requires explicit actions such as New Daily Log, New Order, Create Week, or Add Item. Save on existing commit events; preserve text and dirty state while persistence is pending. Failed actions remain visible as failures.
  • Accounts are admin-created through the established email setup flow. Resend Invite issues a fresh setup link and invalidates the earlier link; Send Password Reset is a distinct action. No public self-registration is part of the current product.
  • Jobs require a number, name, and job type; field assignments can come later. Optional settings include GC, dates, address, burden, tax exemption, certification, CIP, and KJIC. Blank burden defaults to 0.33; tax exemption and certification start false. Keep managed reference lists and existing validation.
  • Global employees have first/last name, employee number, wage, occupation, and contractor status. Draft linked records may reflect updated employee information; submitted records retain their snapshot until intentionally changed. One-off timecard employees remain separate from the global list, and deleting a weekly card must not delete a global employee.
  • Weekly timecards cover Sunday through Saturday and preserve the Excel H/P/C mental model and exact output. Admin/Payroll export and lock access, submitted snapshots, and after-submission audit history are protected behavior.
  • Shop Orders retain fast worksheet entry, nested catalog browsing, custom one-off items, today-or-future delivery dates, and the Thursday shortcut. Submission locks field-user editing. Normal and custom items share a continuous print table with repeating headers; the attached PDF remains the reliable print artifact. A fulfillment dashboard is future scope.
  • Daily Logs retain their field groups and require populated values, including an explicit N/A where appropriate, for submission. Recorded requirements restrict creation/editing/submission to the current day, allow multiple logs for the same job/date, and keep submitted records read-only for foremen. Preserve existing submitted text in emails.
  • Daily Log photos stay grouped by their original section, including normal Photos, PTP, and QC. The recorded email contract uses up to six lightweight inline JPEG thumbnails per section in upload order, descriptions, and a section-specific full-gallery action for overflow. The public gallery must expose every image through existing unguessable share links and scroll on phones, tablets, and desktops. Do not attach the full gallery images to email.

Access and notification policy

RoleRecorded baseline
AdminFull access, including users, employees, jobs, catalog, settings, exports, and administration.
PayrollEmployees, timecard export/locking, job creation, and read-only job lookup. Post-creation job editing remains an open business question.
Shop ForemanCatalog management, all-job read-only lookup, and Shop job workflows. Broader job/setup scope requires a confirmed decision.
Project ManagerAssigned-job setup/workspace access, all-job lookup, and submitted timecard reporting for assigned jobs; no job deletion/archive. Additional submission/export rights remain subject to the recorded questions.
ForemanAssigned-job field workflows. No user/employee administration, catalog administration, or payroll export.
Inactive / noneNo authenticated workspace access.

Use shared capability helpers consistently across navigation, route guards, services, functions, and rules. UI visibility alone is not authorization. Resolve job assignment from the actual job record where required by existing policy.

Daily Log and Shop Order recipients combine protected admin global/job entries, job-specific field-user entries, and assigned active Foremen, Shop Foremen, and Project Managers. Normalize, deduplicate, and reject invalid addresses; field users cannot modify protected admin entries. Admin, Payroll, and no-access users are not automatic field recipients unless explicitly configured. Preserve current Timecard recipient policy.

The existing All Jobs recipient panel owns global new-job and field-assignment email defaults. New-job messages include initial assignees; later assignment messages respond to added users, not removals or ordinary edits. Leased event claims reduce duplicate sends, but delivery and completion recording are not an atomic transaction.

Architecture and data ownership

  • Use Vue 3/TypeScript, Pinia, Vue Router, Firebase services/functions, and selectively wrapped unstyled PrimeVue primitives. Route views orchestrate; components accept props and emit intent; feature composables own reusable behavior; stores own cross-page state; services own Firebase SDK access, normalization, validation, and E2E runtime branches.
  • Preserve existing import boundaries. Shared/rendering components should not gain direct service, store, or Firebase dependencies. Keep policy in pure helpers; keep subscription and browser-event cleanup explicit. Maintain existing test IDs and public props/events/slots.
  • Shared foundations live under src/styles with main.css as the entry point. Tokens, reset/base rules, utilities, and vendor adjustments remain global; component and feature styles stay with their owners. Exact print/email/PDF CSS stays separate.
  • Data domains include users, jobs, employees, managed reference lists, module recipients, timecardWeeks/cards/auditEntries, dailyLogs, shopCatalogNodes, and shopOrders/items. These names summarize the former schema plan; deployed rules, services, and types determine actual paths and compatibility needs.
  • Scope and paginate queries, maintain needed indexes, validate runtime payloads, use server timestamps, preserve immutable submitted snapshots, and record actor/submission information. Avoid large client-side filtering reads as a new default.
  • Cloud Functions own privileged lifecycle operations, submission, email, and exact output generation. Await asynchronous work, clean temporary files, validate authorization server-side, and use operation IDs/status records and idempotency where retries matter. Do not log complete emails, setup/reset links, tokens, or attachment bytes.
  • The August 20 Daily Log attachment decision keeps parent-record authorization in Firestore Rules and callables. Storage independently validates authenticated creation using path, uploader UID, metadata, type, and size; updates are denied. Do not reintroduce Storage-to-Firestore authorization joins for that path as a styling change. Existing read/delete access and public share behavior remain separate concerns.

Verification and release boundaries

Choose checks for the files and behavior actually changed: type-check/build plus relevant unit and Playwright coverage for application changes; output smoke tests for rendering changes; direct rules validation for rules changes. Validate mobile/short-laptop layouts, keyboard focus, labels, saving/empty/error states, and print isolation. A documentation-only cleanup does not claim a fresh app or production audit.

Useful existing commands: npm run type-check, npm run build, targeted npm run test:unit -- --run ... and npm run test:e2e -- ..., and the Daily Log/Shop Order/Timecard smoke scripts. Keep source and generated function artifacts consistent when functions actually change.

Do not combine visual work with role-policy, rules, schema, email, or PDF changes. Before deleting compatibility data, identify readers, writers, rules, indexes, migrations, and deployed consumers. Firebase releases need an intentional order and rollback plan. Commit, push, deploy, and outbound messages are separate actions, not implied by this document cleanup.

Historical carry-over to verify before reopening

The former execution board records the main refactor closed through R688. It separately lists R08 (direct Rules emulator suite) as deferred and R689?R692 for compact-laptop catalog usability, public gallery scrolling, photo-section grouping in email, and delivery-control containment. Later UI work may already cover these items; confirm remaining need against current code and tests before treating them as new tasks. Historical passing counts are not results from this cleanup.

Open business decisions

  • Whether Project Managers can export assigned-job timecards to PDF/CSV, receive timecard emails, or create/submit Daily Logs and Shop Orders beyond current behavior.
  • Whether Payroll can edit jobs after creation, and whether Shop Foremen can edit Shop setup fields or use non-Shop assignments.
  • The meaning and data types of CIP and KJIC.
  • Whether to introduce promotion of a one-off timecard employee to the global list in a future version. The recorded first-version direction leaves that out.

Custom non-admin roles, customizable dashboards/widgets, a file drive, announcements, analytics, broader authentication changes, and a shop fulfillment workspace remain future ideas. They are not requirements for the present design rollout. Admin retains full access.

Image provenance and generation prompt

The construction photograph is an AI-generated concept made September 9, 2026 and used temporarily at sign-in. It does not depict a Phase 2 project. The architectural blueprint artwork was generated the same day with the built-in image generation tool and now appears behind the login form. It replaces the smoky artwork; the superseded application asset has been removed.

Current application assets: src/assets/images/construction-placeholder.webp and src/assets/images/login-blueprint.webp. The photograph embedded in this guide is an exact copy of the former. The construction photograph retains its 20% dark overlay. Login controls and the green timecard workspaces are unchanged.

Final generation prompt

Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: original decorative background for the login panel of Phase 2, a professional construction company's web application. Create a portrait raster image, 1024 by 1536 pixels.
Primary request: a refined architectural blueprint illustration that feels crafted and confident, with crisp, restrained linework and generous quiet space.
Scene and subject: layered architectural fragments of commercial construction, including wall framing, an elegant building corner in axonometric perspective, and ceiling or facade details. Drawn as fine technical lines, composed artistically rather than as a literal working plan.
Composition: drawing details concentrated along the upper-right edge and lower-left edge, with occasional fine lines around the perimeter. Keep the central area from x=20% to 80%, y=28% to 73% very quiet, dark, and nearly empty for readable login headings and fields. Edge details should remain attractive when cropped on mobile.
Color palette: predominantly a flat deep ink navy near #112838. Architectural lines in muted company blue #00437F and subdued pale sky blue #8BC4E8, low to moderate contrast. Use burnt orange #B65326 very sparingly on a handful of structural edges or drafting marks, less than 5% of the image.
Style and mood: premium architectural editorial artwork; precise fine strokes with subtle weight variations, minimal, grounded, clean. Matte navy background with at most a very fine paper texture. Depth comes from overlapping drawings rather than shading.
Constraints: artwork only, with no text, lettering, numbers, labels, dimensions, logo, watermark, UI, buttons, or form. No smoke, ribbons, neon, glow, lens flare, futuristic HUD, circuit-board motifs, heavy gradients, dense all-over grid, or photographic buildings. Keep the negative space intentional and uncluttered.
Workspace artwork, generation prompts, and styling boundary

Application styling

src/styles/brand-workspace.css holds the shared brand styles. AppShell.vue shares navigation, the outer page background, dialogs, and notifications through app-shell--branded. app-shell--branded-content applies the content theme to core routes while timecard and export workspaces keep their original inherited tokens. The green workspace has an opaque backing in its original background color, so the navy page background does not tint it. Workbook fonts, controls, geometry, and behavior remain unchanged. The standalone print route and root tokens are unchanged.

The logo is an unchanged copy of the existing company mark. The three application font files and their SIL Open Font License notices are stored locally under src/assets/fonts; no external font service is required. This design folder continues to contain only the self-contained HTML source and its shareable PDF.
